events.title: The Scopes "Monkey Trial" Begins
events.description: In Dayton, Tennessee, high school teacher John T. Scopes went on trial for teaching human evolution, which broke a new state law. The case drew huge crowds and reporters from across the country. It was among the first trials to be broadcast live on radio nationwide.
events.significance: The trial turned into a national argument over science, religion and academic freedom. Those themes still shape debates about what schools teach.

events.title: Allied Forces Land in Sicily
events.description: Before dawn, American, British and Canadian troops came ashore on the southern coast of Sicily in Operation Husky. It was one of the largest amphibious assaults of the Second World War.
events.significance: The invasion gave the Allies their first foothold in Axis-held Europe. It helped topple Mussolini and opened the Italian campaign.

events.title: Telstar 1 Is Launched
events.description: A Delta rocket lifted off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, carrying Telstar 1. It was the first active communications satellite and could relay television signals across the Atlantic.
events.significance: Telstar opened the era of live satellite broadcasts between continents. It was a forerunner of today's global communications networks.

events.title: The Bahamas Becomes Independent
events.description: The Bahamas ended centuries of British colonial rule and became a sovereign nation. The date is still celebrated each year as Independence Day.
events.significance: Independence made the Bahamas a self-governing member of the Commonwealth. It was part of the wider postwar wave of decolonization in the Caribbean.

events.title: The Rainbow Warrior Is Sunk in Auckland
events.description: The Greenpeace flagship Rainbow Warrior was moored at Marsden Wharf in Auckland, New Zealand, when explosions sank it. A crew member died. The ship was preparing to protest French nuclear testing in the Pacific.
events.significance: The bombing caused an international scandal and strained relations between France and New Zealand. It also became a landmark moment for the environmental movement.
